title: Regression review
description: The review the regression-coverage-reviewer writes of one regression artifact: the scope before Red (plan review) or the final mapping after Red (mapping review). What each review stage checks, what makes a finding blocking and how a re-review treats the previous review are stated in skills/cumulative-regression/SKILL.md (Independent review). task-to-deploy.js accepts it against this file and corrects the artifact only from a review that names a blocking finding; scripts/portfolio/regression.py validate and verify accept the artifact only with a review that is approved, names no blocking finding and cites evidence.

approved.description: True exactly when no finding is blocking. A non-blocking finding never withholds approval.

previousFindings.description: One ruling on each finding of the previous review the brief names, in that review's order; empty when the brief names no previous review.

finding.description: The previous finding, as the previous review states it.

resolved.description: Whether the artifact under review now resolves it.

evidence.description: Where the artifact resolves it, or what still leaves it unresolved, with the source reference.

findings.description: The findings of this review: each unresolved blocking finding of the previous review again, and each new finding the review stage allows.

severity.description: blocking: the artifact misses or misstates an obligation, so the evidence the gate collects would not prove a current requirement; it fails approval and goes back to the assessor. non-blocking: a note that loses no evidence; it is carried with the review and fails nothing.

finding.description: What is wrong, with the source reference that shows it.

correction.description: The verifiable correction, in terms the regression plan contract can express.

evidence.description: The sources read and what each showed, each with its reference: what the review accepts as well as what it finds; at least one, since regression.py refuses a review that cites no evidence.
